pue.boundary: Global PUE for datacenters Microsoft fully owned and controlled that were operational for the full twelve months of FY2025; excludes leased and colocated sites, commissioning activity, newer capacity and sites outside the coverage rule
pue.basis: Microsoft reports FY2025 global PUE of 1.17 and regional PUE of 1.16 Americas, 1.28 Asia Pacific and 1.16 EMEA. The table is a measured historical owned-fleet proxy, but Microsoft does not disclose the matching facility and IT energy used to weight regions on the PUE page. Table 15 separately reports 15,931,489 MWh for a similar but not proven identical owned-and-controlled FY2025 electricity boundary. Therefore 1.17 is not selected for the Q4 FY2026 Azure AI model and no low/base/high range is invented.
pue.selected_rationale: No Q4 FY2026 PUE matched to all owned, leased, colocated and newly commissioned Azure AI capacity; historical coverage is materially narrower than the revenue perimeter.
pue.aggregation: sum(facility energy)/sum(IT equipment energy), equivalently IT-energy-weighted PUE; regional figures are not simply averaged.

model.revenue_scope: Restated Azure revenue, which includes cloud and AI consumption-based services and virtual desktop offerings; AI attribution is unavailable
model.capacity_time_basis: 91-day average active Azure AI IT MW by owned, leased, colocated and purchased-capacity cohort; the 1 GW added during Q4 is an addition and not an average denominator

formulas.annualized_azure_revenue: Q4 restated Azure revenue * 4; run-rate convention, not a forecast
formulas.average_active_AI_IT_MW: sum(cohort active AI IT MW * active days in Q4)/91 across owned, leased, colocated and purchased capacity
formulas.average_effective_utilized_AI_IT_MW: sum(cohort active AI IT MW * physical utilization * active days in Q4)/91
formulas.revenue_per_IT_MW: Q4 annualized Azure revenue * AI compute attribution / average active AI IT MW / 1e6
formulas.revenue_per_effective_utilized_IT_MW: Q4 annualized Azure revenue * AI compute attribution / average effective utilized AI IT MW / 1e6
formulas.historical_owned_fleet_implied_IT_load: historical average facility MW / 1.17 reported PUE; boundary diagnostic only
formulas.PUE_sensitivity: At fixed facility MW F, AI attribution a and utilization u: annualized Azure revenue*a*PUE/(F*u)/1e6. A higher PUE increases the ratio only because usable IT MW falls; it is not better economics.
formulas.utilization_sensitivity: At fixed active IT MW I and AI revenue R: R/(I*u)/1e6; contracted billing and reserved capacity do not prove physical utilization.
formulas.Jevons: not calculated; Foundry revenue growth and one-trillion-token customer counts lack matching realized token/task price, volume and spend series
formulas.maia_rack_density: 96/(167/1000); design accelerators per MW of rack envelope only
formulas.maia_energy_per_token_reduction: 1-1/1.4 conditional on identical comparison workload and power boundary
formulas.facility_density: rack_density * fraction_of_IT_power_attributable_to_these_racks / matched_operational_PUE; both additional inputs undisclosed
formulas.economic_carry: paid_unaccepted_hardware_capital * financing_rate * delay_days/365; no numerical output without paid cohort and loan mapping
formulas.collateral_shortfall: max(0, secured_exposure + priority_costs - net_eligible_collateral_recovery - enforceable_other_recoveries); jurisdiction, waterfall, market appraisal and guarantee terms required

structured_deals.economic_effect: OpenAI contracted for an incremental $250B of Azure services in October 2025. The April 2026 amendment keeps Microsoft as primary cloud partner but permits OpenAI to serve products on other clouds, ends Microsoft-to-OpenAI revenue share, preserves capped OpenAI-to-Microsoft revenue share through 2030 and makes Microsoft's IP license non-exclusive through 2032. Contract value is not recognized revenue, physical utilization or period-average IT MW.

structured_deals.status: four-tranche contract; first 50 IT MW accepted after FY2026 year-end
structured_deals.economic_effect: $9.6668B maximum fees over four 50 IT MW tranches and an approximately five-year average service term imply $9.67M per stated IT MW-year. The scheduled 20% upfront payment is credited after month 24 and is not current Azure revenue. Acceptance, delay and termination provisions mean contract MW cannot be treated as Q4 FY2026 active or utilized Microsoft capacity. Section3.2.a.v protects minimum fees irrespective of Microsoft utilization, subject to contract exceptions; custom-silicon substitution alone does not establish a termination right.

The original SOW uses acceptance, availability, termination credits and scheduled upfront funding. The January addendum adds tranches with no upfront payment and a monthly GPU fee formula. Redacted GPU counts, rates and schedules prevent translation to Microsoft's active IT MW or effective utilization.

structured_deals.status: 20-year PPA; August6 2026 update targets 2027 restart, not actual operation
structured_deals.economic_effect: The agreement supports restart of an approximately 835 MW nuclear facility and matches energy to Microsoft's PJM datacenter use. Price is undisclosed. Generation MW delivered to the grid is neither Azure IT MW nor PUE and is excluded from the revenue denominator. Original 2028 timing is superseded by the 2027 issuer target after reported interconnection-rights waiver and fuel-license progress.

$443.506B lease payments including imputed interest, $194.060B purchase commitments primarily related to datacenters including open purchase orders and take-or-pay contracts, and $34.566B construction commitments create long-duration fixed funding exposure. Counterparties, power boundaries and AI attribution are not disclosed.

structured_deals.status: Filed form of SOW; effective date and economics redacted or blank
structured_deals.economic_effect: Section1.3 provides 6MW colocation space for Microsoft-supplied CPU/storage/networking alongside GPU services. Do not count it as accelerator-only load or multiply GPU-TDP density across it. Section3.4 technology change is mutually agreed and can adjust acceptance/delivery timing while preserving contract value. Section6.10 replaces generic PO termination provisions with stated cause provisions; no free cancellation inferred.

structured_deals.status: Disclosed June30 balances and FY2026 revenue
structured_deals.economic_effect: Note1 separately discloses $27.8B component-purchase receivables, $11.3B supplier-agreement restricted investments, $24.1B OpenAI commercial revenue inclusive of revenue share and $6B OpenAI receivable. These are different accounting categories; no summation into idle inventory or pure AI compute revenue. Microsoft says it is not primary beneficiary of its VIE investments; no consolidation does not by itself mean no economic exposure.

findings: October12 issuer roadmap targets Maia multi-gigawatt expansion starting2027, with Maia200 already serving production. Maia300 rack design gives 96 accelerators/167kW, or 574.85 accelerators per MW of rack envelope. Not installed fleet MW or PUE.

Expected 40% tokens/MW uplift versus an unspecified leading-GPU baseline conditionally implies 28.57% less energy per equivalent token. The separate up-to7x rack throughput claim compares Maia200. Neither establishes realized price declines, current GPU utilization or collateral impairments.

External Azure consumption and first-party AI workloads have different revenue consequences. $24.1B FY2026 OpenAI commercial revenue includes revenue-sharing payments, so it does not close the pure Azure AI-compute attribution gap.

New extraction of June30 disclosures: $329.1B leases not yet commenced, $27.8B server-component receivables and $11.3B supplier-restricted investments. These indicate commitments and capital tied up, not a measured paid-for idle GPU stock; do not double-count uncommenced leases in the broader lease bucket.

Strongest disconfirming evidence: FY2026 consolidated operating cash flow was $182.9B versus $115.948B cash PPE spending; accepted IREN capacity has minimum fees independent of Microsoft utilization, subject to exceptions. Do not assume Microsoft has a neocloud funding gap or Maia automatically cancels suppliers.
